summary: self-sign 5.6.4 contains hidden eval() backdoor disguised as PEM certificate input
details: The main entrypoint exports a `generate(attrs, options, defaults)` function whose undocumented third parameter is treated as PEM-armored code: the function strips `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`/`-----END CERTIFICATE-----` markers and whitespace, base64-decodes the remaining body, and passes the decoded bytes to `eval()`. Any code path that reaches `generate` with attacker-influenced content in the third argument executes arbitrary JavaScript in the consuming process. The PEM-armor framing has no role in legitimate certificate generation and serves to disguise executable payload as certificate-shaped data. The JSDoc does not document this parameter and the shipped example passes `null` for it, indicating the sink is not part of the advertised API.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
